subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Three-Hour Rule
description: Learn The Three-Hour Rule in one minute.

hook.text: If a train trip takes under three hours, it wins most of the air-rail market. Above four, planes win.

buildup.text: The three-hour threshold reflects total travel time: city center to city center, no airport hassle.

discovery.text: Madrid–Barcelona at 2.5 hours by train took 80% of air passengers. Paris–Nice at 5.5 hours took almost none.

twist.text: This rule shapes where countries build new lines. If three hours isn't achievable, the investment fails.

climax.text: Every proposed high-speed line is tested against this rule. Break it, and ridership forecasts collapse.

punchline.text: Three hours is rail's magic number.

quiz.question: What happens when a high-speed train trip takes under three hours?
options: It captures most of the air-rail market
